sink.request_body_format: application/x-www-form-urlencoded canonical media play request body

task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after stage routing, pin/queue gating and input preparation, whose own body rewrites the media play form fields plus a derived signature into the target observable request body rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the console sink or fetch call.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: local DOM event plane on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name request_body and the fetch endpoint and method are assembled from adjusted character-code arrays, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The canonical request body is produced by one reducer instance selected at runtime from 44 near-identical reducer configs.
The commit route selects its live reducer slot only after submit-time form, tuple and runtime state are captured.

The submit path crosses a two-step staged form submission, switch-based action routing, gate checks, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot selection, request-body construction, console emission and fetch dispatch.
The same commit interaction emits non-target media.shadow.action objects before the target media.play object.
The bundle contains 44 high-similarity reducer configs plus 25 vendor-noise modules that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target request_body.
The target value is separated from the form submission by async/await, animation-frame, microtask, timer and mutation-observer boundaries plus a local event-plane hop before the reducer runs.
The selected reducer slot is chosen by a state machine over runtime form and shadow state, not statically.
The console sink and fetch call both receive an already-constructed request body, so sink inspection or fetch interception alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: submit-time media play form fields rewritten into a canonical fetch request body
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a deterministic canonical request body that rewrites the media play form fields (filter, playlist, quality) plus a derived signature, emitted to console.log under action media.play and sent as the body of a POST fetch to /api/media/play.

near_categories.why_not: The target is a rewritten request body string, not a browser/media fingerprint hash.
The target is the whole rewritten request body, not an opaque proof/seal token; the embedded sig is one field of the body.
The transform rewrites form string fields into a canonical request body string, not a binary buffer.
